#### Background and Data {#sec-pmd-631}

[**Description of Data Collection**]{#sec-pmd-631-collection}

The ultrasonic reference block data consist of a response variable and a predictor variable. The response variable is ultrasonic response and the predictor variable is metal distance.

These data were provided by the NIST scientist Dan Chwirut.

[**Software**]{#sec-pmd-631-software}

The analyses used in this case study can be generated using both Dataplot code and R code.<!-- XREF: Dataplot macro not migrated; source handbook/pmd/section6/pmd631.dp --> The R code reproduced throughout this case study follows NIST's own reference R script for it.

::: {.callout-note}
NIST's original page links the downloadable data file for this case study to `CHWIRUT2.DAT`, a NIST Statistical Reference Dataset of only 54 observations that is explicitly documented (in its own header) as "a subset of CHWIRUT1.DAT." However, the 214-observation data table displayed on NIST's page, and the `resp`/`dist` vectors hard-coded into NIST's own reference R script for this case study, both match the full `CHWIRUT1.DAT` dataset instead, not the linked `CHWIRUT2.DAT` file. `CHWIRUT1.DAT` is not included among the data files distributed with the handbook. For this book, the 214-observation dataset has been reconstructed directly from the vectors embedded in NIST's reference R script (confirmed to exactly reproduce every fitting result reported throughout this case study) and is provided as `CHWIRUT1.DAT` alongside the rest of the book's [downloaded data](../../datasets/CHWIRUT1.DAT).
:::

[**Resulting Data**]{#sec-pmd-631-data}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

chwirut <- read_table(
  here::here("datasets", "CHWIRUT1.DAT"),
  skip = 25,
  col_names = c("response", "metal_distance")
)

chwirut
```
